rationale: This is the final iteration, so the candidate should be the best design the evidence supports, not a new experiment. Iteration 10 (kd 0.25, everything else as the iteration 1 baseline) is the best raced design at 81.25, up from 75.97. Its oval progress rose to 0.206 from 0.159, its s-bend steering_oscillation fell to 0.21 from 0.23, and its s-bend progress fell only slightly, to 0.276 from 0.295. Over the kd sweep, s-bend progress was 0.155 at kd 0.1 and 0.15, 0.29 at kd 0.2, and 0.276 at kd 0.25. The kd trend has therefore flattened, with the gain now coming from the oval and lower jitter. Every other lever tested (base_speed 1.2 and 1.5, kp 2.5, wider sensor spacing, sensor_size 0.016) lowered the score, and max_error stayed at 0.061 to 0.065 under all of them. I considered kd 0.3, but the s-bend result already shows the progress peak is near 0.2 to 0.25, and an untested value on the final unseen track is an avoidable risk. I therefore submit the raced iteration 10 design unchanged: kp 2.0, kd 0.25, ki 0, base_speed 1.4, sensors at x -0.02..0.02 and y 0.04, sensor_size 0.012, weights -2..2, and last_direction line loss. Expected result: a score near 81 on the development tracks, with the final race's result depending on how well the unseen track resembles the oval and s-bend. The off-track failure (max_error about 0.06 to 0.065) is not fixed by any lever tested, so the run will probably still end off track. Measurements requested: progress, max_error and where it peaks, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and completion_time per track, so the final result can be compared with the development evidence.
